references.text: The closest parallel to Lot's offer: the host in Gibeah offers his virgin daughter and the guest's concubine to the men outside to protect his guests, an almost identical situation.
Lot followed the same duty of hospitality as Abraham – the guests had come 'under his roof' (betsél qoratí), and he felt obligated to protect them at all costs.
The exhortation about showing hospitality to strangers, for some have unknowingly entertained angels as guests – directly relevant to Lot's situation where the guests were angels.
The tragic consequences of Lot's offer and his flight from Sodom: his daughters later took matters into their own hands, illustrating the long-term effects of the family's experiences.
Peter describes the righteous Lot who was tormented by the lawless people's shameful conduct, highlighting Lot's moral anguish in this situation.
This is a parallel account of the same event (the fall of Sodom) that illuminates Lot's desperate attempt to protect his guests by sacrificing his daughters.
